result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with a marked zebra crosswalk and basic sidewalk infrastructure. While a traffic signal is present, the street width and lack of pedestrian-specific safety enhancements like bulb-outs or refuge islands increase exposure risk.

hazards.name: Wide crossing distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway increases the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic without a refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway at the zebra crossing.

hazards.name: Lack of visible pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are clearly visible to provide safe crossing intervals.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install signal heads with countdown timers to provide pedestrians with clear information on crossing time.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with marked zebra crosswalks and pedestrian signals, providing a baseline level of safety. However, the lack of physical traffic calming measures and some pavement degradation in the crossing area present risks to pedestrians.

hazards.name: Pavement degradation
hazards.description: Visible cracking and uneven surfaces within the intersection and crosswalk area.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from vegetation
hazards.description: Dense trees on the right corner may obscure pedestrians waiting to cross from the view of approaching motorists.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pavement Repair
interventions.description: Resurface the intersection to eliminate tripping hazards and improve the integrity of the crosswalk markings.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles receive a green light.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with row houses and a marked zebra crosswalk. While sidewalks are present on both sides, the crossing is uncontrolled and lacks physical safety enhancements like curb extensions, leaving pedestrians exposed to traffic with limited visibility due to parked cars.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross two lanes of traffic without the protection of a stop sign or signal at this intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground crosswalk across the main roadway

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Vehicles parked immediately adjacent to the crosswalk limit sightlines between approaching drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right and left curbsides near the foreground crosswalk

hazards.name: Pavement Degradation
hazards.description: Cracking and wear in the asphalt and crosswalk markings may create minor tripping hazards or reduce visibility.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20 feet of the crosswalk to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalk to the level of the sidewalk to act as a speed table and increase pedestrian prominence.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks and a marked crosswalk, but lacks modern safety enhancements like ADA-compliant curb ramps or dedicated pedestrian signals. Visibility is partially obstructed by a large vehicle parked near the corner, and the environment is characterized by aging infrastructure and overhead utility lines.

hazards.name: Lack of ADA Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The sidewalk at the corner lacks a sloped transition, creating a significant barrier for individuals with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Bottom left corner where the sidewalk meets the roadway.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: A large food truck parked close to the intersection blocks the view between pedestrians waiting to cross and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street, parked near the intersection.

hazards.name: Absence of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, requiring pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals which may not provide sufficient crossing time.
hazards.location_in_image: Traffic signal pole on the left corner.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramp Installation
interventions.description: Install tactile, sloped curb ramps at all intersection corners to ensure universal accessibility.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Implement parking restrictions near the intersection to improve sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing transverse crosswalk markings to high-visibility continental-style markings.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to improve safety and predictability for people crossing.
